title: Audit recorded v1
description: DRAFT, proposed by notification, waits for account, payment, provisioning and project. Owner: notification (owner's decision of 10 November 2026: Notification owns the admin activity feed). Serves the admin activity log of the UI (ActivityEntry in webblock-web-ui src/features/admin/monitoring/types.ts). One shape for every producer: each service sends <service>.audit_recorded.v1 on its own exchange (account.events, payment.events, provisioning.events, project.events) with routing key equal to message_type, persistent, application/json, AMQP type = message_type, after the database commit. Which actions each producer sends: account SUSPEND_USER and REACTIVATE_USER; payment CHANGE_PLAN; provisioning SUSPEND_HOSTING, RESUME_HOSTING and ROLLBACK; project sends the same hosting actions only for a change it starts itself and Provisioning does not report (agree with Provisioning so one action is never sent twice). An action that moves through several results (QUEUED, RUNNING, then SUCCEEDED or FAILED) sends one event per result, all with the same activity_id and requested_at and a growing activity_version; an action that is done at once sends one event with activity_version 1. Notification keeps one entry per activity_id and drops an event whose activity_version is at or below the one it holds, so repeats and late messages are harmless. The producer fills in the names the UI shows (actor_email, target_name, target_detail) at the time of the action, so Notification never looks them up. project_id is sent when the target is a website and left out otherwise (open point of envelope.v1 in the README). No passwords, tokens, notes or reasons typed by an admin.

occurred_at.description: When the action reached this result.

project_id.description: The website, when target_type is PROJECT (then it equals target_id). Left out otherwise.

activity_id.description: The action, stable across its results (for example the producer's audit row id or command id). It is the entry id the UI shows.

activity_version.description: Grows by one with each result of the same activity_id.

action.description: The UI's ActivityAction. A new action needs the UI type first, then a new schema version.

requested_at.description: When the action was asked for; the same in every event of one activity_id. The UI shows it as createdAt.

actor_user_id.description: The admin's Keycloak subject; null exactly when actor_type is SYSTEM.

actor_email.description: The admin's email at the time of the action; null exactly when actor_type is SYSTEM.

target_type.description: USER for SUSPEND_USER, REACTIVATE_USER and CHANGE_PLAN (the plan's owner); PROJECT for the hosting actions.

target_name.description: What the UI shows as the target: the user's full name, or the website's name.

target_detail.description: The UI's targetDetail: the user's email for a USER target, the website's domain for a PROJECT target (empty when the website has none yet).
